questions.prompt: Why is a density matrix useful when one statevector is not enough?

options.text: It can represent pure states, mixtures and subsystem descriptions
It always has only two entries
It is only a list of sampled counts

questions.explanation: Density matrices describe pure states as well as classical mixtures, noisy ensembles and reduced subsystems.

questions.prompt: How is the density matrix of a pure state |ψ> constructed?

options.text: The absolute value of each amplitude

questions.explanation: The outer product |ψ><ψ| produces the full matrix of amplitude products.

questions.prompt: What do computational-basis diagonal entries of ρ represent?

options.text: Probabilities for the corresponding basis outcomes

questions.explanation: The diagonal entry ρii is the probability of outcome i in that basis.

questions.prompt: What information is carried by an off-diagonal entry?
questions.explanation: Off-diagonal terms retain relationships between amplitudes that can later affect interference.

questions.prompt: What is different about the Bell state and an equal classical 00/11 mixture?

options.text: The mixture has Bell coherence terms too
The Bell state has 00-to-11 off-diagonal coherence; the mixture does not
Only the mixture has trace one

questions.explanation: Both have the same Z probabilities, but only the coherent Bell state has the corresponding off-diagonal terms.

questions.prompt: What is the purity Tr(ρ²) of an ideal pure state density matrix?
questions.explanation: A pure density matrix satisfies ρ²=ρ, so its purity is Tr(ρ)=1.

questions.prompt: What operation gives the state of one subsystem from ρAB?

options.text: A partial trace over the other subsystem
A second measurement of both systems

questions.explanation: ρA = TrB(ρAB) sums over the basis of the subsystem that is discarded.

questions.prompt: What does ρA=I/2 for one qubit of a Bell pair imply?

options.text: The joint pair is definitely a classical mixture
The local qubit has random one-qubit outcomes, while joint correlations may remain

questions.explanation: A maximally mixed reduced state fixes local predictions but does not erase joint correlations or coherence.

questions.prompt: Why can a basis change distinguish two preparations with the same Z histogram?

options.text: It reveals how off-diagonal coherence combines amplitudes
It reads the hidden classical coin directly

questions.explanation: A basis change can turn coherence into measurable population differences; the diagonal alone does not contain that information.
